record.context_brief: Spectral theory for randomized average mixing matrices
record.original_question: Develop a spectral graph theory for the matrix McR associated with an arbitrary random variable R, where McR = E[M(R)] = integral from minus infinity to infinity of M(t) fR(t) dt, M(t) = U(t) o U(-t), and U(t) = exp(itA) is the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on the graph.

evidence.quote: If R is a random variable with probability density function fR(t) : R −→ [0,∞), then the average mixing matrix under R is defined as McR := E[M(R)] = Z ∞ −∞ M(t)fR(t) dt.
4.6 Open Problem. Develop a spectral graph theory for the matrix McR, R an arbitrary random variable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and let $U(t) = \exp(itA)$ be the transition matrix of the continuous-time quantum walk on $G$. Define the mixing matrix at time $t$ by
$$M(t) = U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)} = U(t) \circ U(-t),$$
where $\circ$ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. For a real-valued random variable $R$ with probability density function $f_R : \mathbb{R} \to [0,\infty)$, define the average mixing matrix under $R$ by
$$\widehat{M}_R := \mathbb{E}[M(R)] = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} M(t)\, f_R(t)\, dt.$$
Develop a spectral graph theory for the matrix $\widehat{M}_R$ where $R$ is an arbitrary random variable. In particular, characterize the eigenvalues, eigenspaces, rank, support, and combinatorial/algebraic invariants of $\widehat{M}_R$ in terms of the spectral decomposition of $A$ and the distribution of $R$, and determine how the choice of distribution $f_R$ influences these invariants.
artifact.category_tag: Average mixing matrices in quantum walks
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2023–2024) on average mixing matrices for continuous-time quantum walks—including work on reversible Markov chains and Szegedy walks—still focuses on specific distributions (uniform time averaging, exponential/Cesàro sampling) and on properties for particular graph families. No source found that develops a general spectral graph theory of $\widehat{M}_R$ for arbitrary random variables $R$; the question appears to remain an open program.

status_evidence.title: Average Mixing in Quantum Walks of Reversible Markov Chains
status_evidence.snippet: Formula for the mixing matrix in terms of the spectral decomposition; relationships with the Szegedy walk.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work develops spectral results for specific averaging schemes, not for arbitrary R.

status_evidence.title: A New Perspective on the Average Mixing Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Studies average mixing matrix via spectral idempotents under standard time averaging.
status_evidence.claim: Existing perspectives address the classical Cesàro-type average, not general densities f_R.

status_evidence.title: A Quantum Walk Mixing Average Mixing Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Properties of the average mixing matrix as a doubly-stochastic matrix encoding time-averaged behavior.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational work treats the standard average; general-R theory not developed.
